title: How this project was driven
note: Human-directed, agent-built. Dates are UTC. No verbatim prompts, no personal data. Actors: human (project owner), planner (reviewing agent), builder (build lead agent), subagent (delegated task agent).

entries.summary: Asked for a neutral study of the WebMCP specification, Chrome documentation, ChatGPT site tools, the showcase, and the challenge rules before choosing a product.
entries.outcome: The research established the API contract, browser differences, secure-context needs, and submission constraints.

entries.summary: Proposed a live meeting architecture whiteboard and asked for a critical assessment.
entries.outcome: The idea was rejected because it overlapped existing whiteboards and did not need WebMCP. The pointing and shared-selection insight was kept.

entries.summary: Ran an adversarial comparison of about fifteen candidates against the official judging criteria.
entries.outcome: Generic dashboards and cross-site workflows were removed. The chosen product had to depend on live unsaved page state and page-owned deterministic actions.

entries.summary: Checked a manufacturing containment review against practitioner needs and existing products.
entries.outcome: The concept was narrowed and kept only as a fallback because its three-minute story was harder to explain.

entries.summary: Chose a restaurant ordering exception workflow for a clearer demo and a broader audience.
entries.outcome: The live-state pattern moved to a supplier order sheet where signals, pins, preview, adoption, and receipt are visible together.

entries.summary: Re-read the rules and WebMCP documentation, computed the deterministic data, and wrote the build brief and review checklist.
entries.outcome: Cutoff, its five tools, the ten-line data set, the expected totals, and the three review checkpoints were locked.

entries.summary: Wrote failing tests first, then implemented the seed data, pure order engine, revisioned store, and thin WebMCP adapters.
entries.outcome: The engine reproduced the exact table. Stale writes, preview invalidation, adoption, undo, receipt storage, and registration lifecycle passed deterministic tests.

entries.summary: Clarified that checkpoint times define order rather than deadlines and added official model-backed evals to the preview stage.
entries.outcome: Quality gates stayed intact. Static evals measure the required first read, while browser evals measure full ordered chains against live state.

entries.summary: Ran Review 1 tests and the locked flow over local HTTPS in system Chrome and the in-app browser.
entries.outcome: The exact 910-cover, 76-hour, 2,767-unit preview passed. Tool registration changed from four tools to five during preview and returned to four after adoption.

entries.summary: Passed Review 1 and found one state-lifecycle defect plus small annotation, date-copy, and artifact-hygiene issues.
entries.outcome: Row focus became view-only, tool annotations now match their outputs, fixed dates are explicit, and generated browser artifacts are ignored.

entries.summary: Completed the styled order sheet, all eight panels, keyboard controls, receipt actions, activity log, trajectory route, and storage hardening.
entries.outcome: The security review found no high-severity issue. Storage bounds and exception handling gained regression coverage.

entries.summary: Ran the preview flow, independent agent trials, the official eval suites, and the available audit command.
entries.outcome: Sonnet passed 8 of 8 first calls and 17 of 17 browser steps. Gemini 3.7 Flash passed 8 of 8 first calls. A clean Sol run completed the full tool flow. Failed zero-score attempts remain recorded. Ora stopped before scoring because its current CLI and service use different capture versions.

entries.summary: Repeated the deployed flow by hand and passed Review 2 for the builder-owned work. The review found two small product gaps.
entries.outcome: The signal form now explains an empty label. Managers can create the same local handoff receipt through visible controls or the agent tool.

entries.summary: Prepared the local Review 3 package and verified the two Review 2 fixes before updating the preview.
entries.outcome: All 43 tests and the production build passed. The README, timed demo plan, Devpost draft, changelog, trajectory, and MIT license are ready for the final external checks.

entries.summary: Traced a human Chrome inspector failure after successful adoption to immediate dynamic-tool unregistration.
entries.outcome: The adapter now returns the adoption result before unregistering the tool. A regression test covers the ordering, all 43 tests pass, and the corrected preview is live.

entries.summary: Accepted the external Gemini outage after reviewing the combined Chrome, in-app browser, Sonnet, gateway Gemini, and inspector evidence.
entries.outcome: Review 2 closed without more manual retries. Review 3 moved to the public repository and submission-package checks.

entries.summary: Published the audited package to the approved public repository and checked the live GitHub record.
entries.outcome: The default branch is main, GitHub recognizes the MIT license, local and remote commits match, and private build references are absent.
